story_text:
Await is a film-inspired digital camera that turns moments into meaningful prints via its App. Inspired by retro tech toys and pop icons from the '90s, it reimagines the classic camera archetype to make photography playful and intentional again.
## Fewer, meaningful photos
Await blends the playful soul of retro toys with the design of early consumer electronics: translucent plastic, exposed internals, one button that does one thing. Because a camera should capture the moment, not take you out of it.
## A retro-inspired design that stays memorable
Await blends retro toys and consumer devices aesthetic with a playful, pop-driven soul, reinterpreting 20th-century nostalgia for a Gen Z audience drawn to icons they never experienced firsthand.
## The Await look
To us, photography is an act of love towards real moments. The Await filter has been tested across thousands of pictures and dozens of light, shade, and low-light conditions, fine-tuned to enhance the content of every frame in any scenario.
The look is the result of an extensive study of vintage photographs and films, translating the honesty of analog imagery into a consistent digital signature.
Indoor, flash on.
Club, flash off.
Outdoor night party, flash on.
Club, flash on.
Mixed scenario. Partially indoor, partially outdoor. Flash off.
Outdoor, sunny. Flash off.
## Free Await App
The Await App ships on both iOS and Android, so every user can develop, manage, and print rolls from the device they already carry.
## How it works
Await camera and its App work as a single system.
The Camera holds up to 3 rolls of 24 frames (72 pictures total); once full, a sync develops every roll through our custom-designed, vintage-inspired filter, empties the camera, and frees it for the next session.
## The Await experience
## Prints worth awaiting
A photograph isn't fully finished until it lives outside the screen. We work with trusted print partners to bring your favorite frames to your door as high-quality prints on premium paper, handled with the same care you took capturing them.
## Memories vs Files
Photography became a habit. Phone out, shutter down, swipe up, repeat. We called it documenting our lives, but we were just feeding a library nobody opens. Doom photography.
## Intentional vs Mindless
Await Camera is the correction. You decide before the shutter, then put it down and you're back in the moment.
A print finds a place in the world. A camera roll grows quietly in the cloud, full of near-identical shots no one remembers.
Photography should serve the moment, not become one.
## Printing costs
*check shipping costs to your country here https://await.camera/pricing/
These prices only go down.
Await is a community. The more of us shooting and printing every month, the better the rates we negotiate with print labs around the world — and the lower these prices drop. What you see today is our starting point, not our ceiling. Grow the community, shrink the price.
## Print formats
- Await: 150 x 100 mm (6 x 4 in)
- 35mm lab prints: 150 x 100 mm (6 x 4 in)
- Polaroid i-Type / 600: 79 × 79 mm image area (3.1 × 3.1 in) inside a white frame
- Instax Mini: 46 × 62 mm image area (1.8 × 2.4 in), credit-card sized
- Instax Wide: ~62 × 99 mm image area, roughly 2× Instax Mini
- Kodak Mini Shot: 53 × 86 mm standard (2.1 × 3.4 in)
## No app? No problem
You can download the original photos without any filters or compression by connecting the camera directly to your PC or smartphone. Please note that if you download them through the app, the original files will no longer exist there, as the app automatically converts them.
## Await Camera anatomy
1 – Shutter button: press once to shoot. Hold 3 sec to power on/off.
2 – Function button: single press toggles flash. Hold 1.5 sec to toggle timer.
3 – Optical viewfinder: window to frame your shot.
4 – OLED display: rear screen showing battery, timer, flash, rolls, and pictures left.
5 – Xenon flash: diffuser for the integrated xenon flash.
6 – 8MP Sony Sensor: fixed lens focusing light onto the sensor.
7 – Sounding buzzer: internal speaker for shutter, timer, and system audio feedback.
8 – Magnetic faceplate: swappable front plate held by magnets for colorway changes.
9 – Strap holes: side-mounted attachment points for wrist or neck straps.
10 – USB-C port: recharge the camera.
11 – Threaded mount: attach the camera to a tripod.
12 – Torx screws: openable design, expandable for future add-ons.
## OLED Screen
- Battery level: current charge of the internal battery (4 bars max, each bar ≈ 25%).
- Timer 10 sec.: self-timer enabled. Press the shutter to start a 10-second countdown before the camera fires.
- Xenon flash: await Camera uses a true xenon gas-discharge tube, the same technology found in classic film cameras and pro studio strobes. It produces a brief, intense, daylight-balanced burst that freezes motion and delivers the authentic analog flash look LED cannot replicate.
- Rolls left: digital rolls remaining before processing (3/3 = three full rolls available).
- Pics left: exposures left in the current roll (24/24 = fresh roll, no shots taken).
## Tech specs
- Sensor: 8MP Sony IMX179 CMOS sensor (1/3.2", 3264 × 2448) with a fixed f/2.0 lens at 2.8 mm (≈26 mm equiv.), ~65–72° diagonal field of view.
- Bluetooth: 5.2 LE, 2402–2480 MHz, 0.99 dBm EIRP
- Wi-Fi: 2.4 GHz 802.11 b/g/n, 2412–2472 MHz, 16.09 dBm EIRP
- Battery: Lithium polymer CLY803040, 3.7 V nominal, 4.2 V charge, 1000 mAh
- Charging: USB-C, CC/CV
- SAR: 0.872 W/kg (1g, FCC) · 0.179 W/kg (10g, CE/UKCA)
- Ongoing certifications: FCC, CE, UKCA
## Pocketable by design
Await covers a footprint just ~44% larger than a credit card.
Size: 98 × 68 × 15 mm (3.86 × 2.68 × 0.59 in)
Weight: 92.7 g (3.27 oz)
## Magnetic, Swappable Faceplates
Magnetic, swappable skins enable customization, while a transparent, high-tech language exposes PCBs and the internals as a core aesthetic value.
The body stays the same for everyone; the front skin is where customization happens. Buyers choose a color at checkout and can buy more skins as single add-ons, swapping them magnetically in a snap.
## Accessories
The two Await-branded straps tie into the integrated loops: a short wrist strap for one-handed shooting, and a longer cord that wears as a neck strap or crossbody, keeping the camera close to the body and always within reach.
## Pair them with the Camera
1 — Separate the parts
The strap ships in two pieces: the strap with quick-release clip, and a small cord buckle that anchors to the camera body.
2 — Thread the cord
Pass the thin cord loop through the strap hole on the side of the camera.
3 — Lock the buckle
Pull the plastic clip end back through the cord loop to secure the connector.
4 — Clip the strap
Snap the strap onto the connector. Ready to wear.
## Build an album of memories you actually chose
We are bringing intentionality back to photography. Await is designed for exactly this, which is why we shot hundreds and hundreds of frames ourselves. We got more quality time out of every moment, and we experienced the difference firsthand.
## 100% Free app experience
The Await app is free. Download your photos, manage your rolls, no fees, no subscription. We ask for a card at onboarding so checkout is one tap when you decide to print a roll. If you don't want to print your rolls, you can enjoy them in your gallery, free of charge.
## Skip the checkout
The moment you finish a roll is the moment you've already decided. We don't want that decision to die at a checkout screen. So we ask for your card once, during onboarding, and from then on printing is one tap.
Nothing is ever charged until you choose to print. Manually, you confirm each roll. In Automatic mode, completed rolls queue for 24 hours before printing, leaving you a window to cancel before anything leaves your account.
## Automatic vs Manual
## Automatic - Best Value
Every synced roll is queued for print and shipped 24h later, with a delivery fee* added to the discounted $8.99 per roll* price. Within that window, users can skip any roll they want to keep digital; after that, the prints are on their way.
## Manual - Print on Demand
Synced rolls stay digital by default; nothing prints unless the user sends it to print. This mode trades the seamless convenience and discounted roll pricing of Automatic for total control, maintaining a $9.99 per roll* price plus a delivery fee*.
*Shipping price may vary by country. check https://await.camera/pricing/
## For lifehackers like us
We're Rolling Square, a Swiss team solving real-life problems through functional, disruptive design. Our Lifehackers community shares the same drive: smart innovation for better everyday life.
Await is our next chapter. A generation is rediscovering film-era rituals and craving photography that feels real, away from phones.
We unveiled it at CES in January 2026, gathered valuable feedback, and developed it through to launch: a film-inspired digital camera that turns moments into meaningful prints, bringing intention, slowness, and physicality back to image-making.
## Media talking about us
Rolling Square is known worldwide for innovative products and bold design, backed by a strong crowdfunding track record and a community of lifehackers and reviewers who love what we build.
Await is where we dared more, taking the same tech-driven, problem-solving DNA of every Rolling Square product and applying it to references we had never touched. Vintage cameras gave us the discipline of a finite roll and the ritual of waiting.
'90s and '00s pop icons like the Poké Ball and the original Instagram logo brought the playful, collectible feel of an era when photography still meant something. Retro toys like the transparent Game Boy Color taught us that a circuit board can be a design statement. All rebuilt through our functional, disruptive lens.
## Rewards
risks: Await is a hardware plus software project, which means the main risks are related to production timelines, software stability, and logistics. On the hardware side, the camera design, electronics, and manufacturing partners are already onboarded, with prototypes validated through multiple revisions. Regulatory certifications (FCC, CE, UKCA) are already in progress and on track for shipping. The remaining risk is related to production lead times and yield consistency. To reduce this, production is being split into controlled batches, with inspections at each stage before moving forward. On the software side, the main challenge is ensuring stable connectivity between the camera and the app, and reliable image transfer and roll development. The app is in active development, and core features are being tested internally before release. We are prioritizing stability over feature count, and will only roll out updates once they meet our quality standards. Logistics and fulfillment can also be affected by external factors such as customs delays or shipping disruptions. To mitigate this, we work with experienced international logistics partners and plan buffer time into the delivery schedule. As with any Kickstarter project, delays are possible. Our commitment is to communicate clearly and early if anything changes, and to keep backers informed at every step.

faq.q: Can Await be used without the app?
faq.a:
Yes. Await works as a standalone digital camera. You can connect it directly to a compatible phone, tablet, or computer via USB-C and access your original, unprocessed photos without using the Await app, creating an account, or using our printing service.
The app is there to make syncing, developing, organizing, and optionally printing your rolls more convenient.

Estimated delivery is Dec 2026. Before we ship, we contact you to confirm your shipping address and pick your colors, so a move or address change is never a problem. We will also email tracking the moment your camera is on the way.

faq.q: Why can I only see my photos after finishing a roll?
faq.a:
That’s intentional. Await is designed around 24-photo rolls to bring back some of the anticipation and intentionality of film photography. When every shot is limited, you naturally think a little more before pressing the shutter.
There’s no artificial waiting period. As soon as you finish your 24 shots, you can develop the roll in the app.
And if you really can’t wait, you can always connect Await via USB-C and access the original files directly. We won’t tell anyone. �

faq.q: Are my photos locked into the Await app?
faq.a:
Not at all. Your photos are yours.
You can download your developed photos from the Await app in full resolution, or connect the camera via USB-C to access the original, unprocessed files directly. You’re also free to print them yourself or use any photo printing service you prefer.

faq.q: Do I need to buy film?
faq.a: Never. Await is digital inside, so there is no film to buy and nothing to reload. You just shoot.

faq.q: How many photos does the camera hold?
faq.a: Up to 3 rolls of 24 frames ,72 pictures total. Once full, a sync with the app (or via cable) develops every roll, empties the camera, and frees it for the next session.

Once you finish a 24-photo roll, you can develop it in the Await app and optionally order physical prints delivered directly to your door.
Before ordering, you can exclude photos you really don’t want printed. Printing is priced per roll, so the price remains the same if you choose to exclude some photos.

faq.q: Where are my prints shipped from?
faq.a: We work with a local print partner in each country, so in most cases your rolls are printed locally, close to you, which means faster delivery and no international shipping on prints.

With Automatic mode, €8.99 per roll of 24, about €0.37 per photo, plus shipping depending on your region (€4.99 for most countries). Manual print-on-demand is at €9.99/roll + shipping. Shipping costs vary by country. You can check your country's shipping cost here: await.camera/pricing
Yes, 100% free, no fees, no subscription. Nothing is ever charged until you choose to print a roll.

faq.q: Can I remove the Await watermark?
faq.a: Yes. The Await watermark can be turned off in the app settings.
Yes. Every pre-order comes with 30-day hassle-free returns and guaranteed delivery. Email support@rollingsquare.com and we will sort it out.
Rolling Square, a Swiss team based in Lugano. Await is our 20th crowdfunding campaign, after $15M+ raised by 280,000+ backers and 750,000+ products delivered, including inCharge and Supertiny.

faq.q: Do I have to use Await's printing service?
faq.a:
No. Printing is completely optional.
You can use Await indefinitely without ever ordering a print. Your digital photos are yours to keep, share, edit, or print wherever you prefer.

updates.title: 🎨 Help us start production early: tell us your colors
Funded in 1 hour. Here's why we built await 📸
updates.text:
Hello, await-ers! 👋
A quick but heartfelt thank you. Await was funded in just 1 hour, and that's all thanks to you. It's our 20th funded campaign, and the first one that's a camera. 😌
We want to take a moment to tell you why we built it.
Somewhere along the way, taking photos stopped being about the moment. We shoot, check, retake, edit, post, and by the time we look up, the sunset is gone, the song is over, the people we were with have moved on. We have thousands of photos and fewer memories of actually being there.
Await is our small act of resistance. No screen. No preview. No retakes. Just…
